Subject: Production impact: large customer facing latency + 5xx spike (BlueRidge)

Hi Tessa —

We started seeing a steady increase in tail latency across Redwood-powered recommendation endpoints at ~08:40 PDT. By 08:50 we began observing ~12% 5xx rates and grossly degraded p95/p99 (p99 > 2.1s vs baseline 0.25s). This is affecting critical checkout personalization flows during a high traffic window — conversion is down ~8%.

Attached a trimmed set of traces and the sampling of failing request IDs. Can your team open a bridge? We need immediate mitigation and an ETA on root cause.

Thanks,
Asha Patel

I'll circulate a readout after the bridge with owners and timeline. We will treat this as an exec-level issue and loop in Laura for any SLA/credits discussion.

Subject: [Bridge notes] BlueRidge outage triage — actions (internal)

On Mon, Jun 14, 2026 at 09:30, Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Standing up bridge — attaching live sampling.

Summary of what we saw on the bridge:
- Root symptom: sudden increase in KV cache eviction rate coincident with a cache node upgrade; this increased upstream latencies for cold KV lookups and caused request timeouts on a subset of long-sequence recommendations.
- Error profile: majority 502/504s from the serving runtime when KV store timeouts propagated; not widespread CPU/GPU saturation.

Immediate actions taken:
- 09:45 PDT: temporarily pinned BlueRidge traffic to stable model variant v2.4.1 (previous is v2.5.0 alpha) — mitigated p99 but did not completely eliminate spikes.
- 09:55 PDT: disabled concurrent aggressive prefetch on checkout route; reduced tail by ~40%
- 10:12 PDT: rolled back a recent cache node configuration change (partial rollback in prod staging first).

Owners and next steps:
- Karthik: full KV eviction analysis & node metrics (ETA 6 hours)
- Grace O'Connor (SRE liaison): validate rollback and run soak tests (ETA 3 hours)
- Tessa/Ben: customer communications and exec summary (ETA 2 hours)

Attachments referenced: perf-sampling-0930.log, blueridge_trimmed-traces-0614.zip

Subject: Post-incident RCA, corrective actions, and follow-through (BlueRidge)

Team and Asha — thanks again for patience while we completed the analysis. Below is a concise RCA, the corrective actions we committed to on the bridge, and the current follow-through tracker.

Executive summary:
- Impact window: 2026-06-14T08:40:00-07:00 to 2026-06-14T10:25:00-07:00
- Users affected: BlueRidge recommendation endpoints (5 consecutive internal checks), customer-visible conversion impact ~8% for 1.75 hours
- Root cause: an automated cache node configuration change deployed during a rolling maintenance window increased eviction churn for a shard group that BlueRidge routes heavily to. The higher eviction rate caused increased cold KV retrievals during generation, triggering timeouts in the serving runtime which surfaced as 502/504.

Corrective actions (completed):
- Rolled back the cache node config change (06-14 09:55 PDT) — mitigated the immediate symptom.
- Pinned BlueRidge to model v2.4.1 for the traffic shape of the day (completed 09:45 PDT).
- Disabled aggressive checkout prefetch flags that were amplifying cold lookups (09:55 PDT).

Planned follow-through (owner / ETA):
- Karthik Iyer / 2026-06-18: deliver KV eviction diagnostic report with shard heatmap and a list of high-risk config knobs. (link: https://drive.redwoodinc/BR/incident-0614/traces)
- Grace O'Connor / 2026-06-20: implement a safety gate for cache node config changes (feature flag + canary threshold).
- Laura Bennett / 2026-06-21: review account SLA exposure and propose targeted credit offer if required.
- Tessa Morgan / 2026-06-18: final RCA doc and customer executive readout prepared (attached).

Attachments: rca-draft-0618.pdf, patch-rollback-plan.txt

Customer response: Asha has confirmed they consider root cause credible and are satisfied with the mitigation cadence and planned safety gates. We will schedule a debrief with BlueRidge execs on 2026-06-22 at 10:00 PDT.

Open notes / risks:
- We observed one other account with similar shard affinity in a test cluster; Karthik to validate isolation and ensure no further noisy-customer risks remain.
- We should add a monitoring alert to detect unusual eviction-rate deltas tied to rolling maintenance.

I'll update the Confluence postmortem and mark items as they close. Please update the tracker with status and estimated completion time.

—Tessa
Director, Priority Accounts — Redwood Inference
